articles.title: Huge crowds greet Pope in Paris ahead of open-air Mass
articles.summary: More than half a million people are expected to attend the event in the heart of the French capital.
articles.body:
Hundreds of thousands of people have greeted Pope Leo XIV in the centre of Paris for a giant open-air Mass.

Crowds cheered as the pontiff moved down the Champs-Élysées Avenue beneath the Arc de Triomphe, waving to crowds from his popemobile.

The head of the Catholic Church blessed several babies as he stopped at different stages along the avenue as chants of "Leo, Leo" rang out.

More than half a million people are expected to attend the event in the heart of the French capital on Saturday and a special altar has been built on the Place de la Concorde for the ceremony.

French President Emmanuel Macron, who met Leo for an hour of talks on Friday, will not be at any of the Pope's Masses during his four-day visit to France, largely to avoid breaching France's strict separation of state and religion.

But the Champs-Élysées Mass will be attended by Macron's wife Brigitte and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu.

Several candidates for next year's presidential election are also expected to attend.

Marine Le Pen of the hard-right National Rally party and conservative Bruno Retailleau were both pictured at the Place de la Concorde ahead of the event, while centrists Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal are also due to be there.

Mayor of Le Havre and former French Prime Minister Edouard Philippe and former Prime Minister Francois Fillon were both also seen at the Place de la Concorde.

Earlier on Saturday, the Pope met migrants as he visited the Maison Bakhita centre, an association supporting refugees, and praised the organisation for inviting "us to see those who are invisible".

During the visit Leo said it was "possible to encounter one another and to live together in dignity and peace".

He also stressed the "the fundamental role of women in building a civilisation of love".

The Pope also issued a warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence (AI) at the start of his visit to France on Friday.

Leo cautioned against "losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines" in wide-ranging remarks to Church and state officials at the Élysée Palace.

Large crowds are expected throughout the pontiff's trip, which the Church believes reflects a growing spirituality among the French and other Europeans.

On Sunday, 150,000 have signed up to attend mass in the Pyrenean sanctuary of Lourdes.

The Pope will be in Metz, in northeast France, on Monday where he will pay tribute to Robert Schuman (1886-1963), a founding father of the European Union and a fervent Catholic who is today a candidate for beatification.

Born in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV was originally called Robert Prevost – a French name.

His paternal grandmother was born in Le Havre in Normandy in 1894. When she married in the US many years later, she and her Italian husband took the name Prevost, which had been her mother's maiden name.

articles.title: Economist calls out America’s socialist elite, says they got rich bashing capitalism
articles.summary: Stephen Moore says Bernie Sanders, Hasan Piker, and Elizabeth Warren grew wealthy under capitalism while pushing socialist policies they call immoral.
articles.body: Socialist and progressive figures have found a lucrative platform attacking capitalism, according to economist Stephen Moore, who says they have grown wealthy inside the free-market system they want to overhaul. Moore, a former senior economic adviser to President Trump, told Fox News Digital in an interview that the United States is uniquely positioned to reward people who criticize capitalism. He said public figures, including Sen. Bernie Sanders and online political commentator Hasan Piker, have benefited from the wealth and opportunities created by the American economy while advocating socialist policies. DSA-BACKED CANDIDATES ARE WINNING PRIMARIES AND THEIR VISION FOR AMERICA IS VERY DIFFERENT "There's no country in the world where you can get rich off of attacking free market capitalism better than in the United States," Moore told Fox Digital. "And so you have dozens of these prominent voices in the socialist movement on the Democratic side who actually are rich, millionaires or more, and they attack the very system that made them rich in the first place." Moore said a recent USA Today opinion piece made a similar argument. The story was titled "Hasan Piker's luxury lifestyle isn't what Marx had in mind." SOCIALIST BIGWIG BLASTS THE WEALTHY WHILE LIVING IN $1.4M BROOKLYN BROWNSTONE WITH EYEBROW-RAISING BACKSTORY It read in part, "America's loudest democratic socialists have a problem: Many of them are too rich. Hasan Piker, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vermont, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Massachusetts, and an entire class of young socialist influencers are all extremely wealthy. Yet even though their wealth was acquired through a capitalist system they see as immoral, they give very little of it away." "It is remarkable how many of these leading, so-called advocates of socialism have come from rich families or have gotten rich on capitalism themselves," Moore said. "So even people like Bernie Sanders are wondering whether there's a degree of hypocrisy here. I mean, there's a reason why just about everybody in the world wants to come to the United States. It's not because we have socialism, it's because we have free market capitalism." THE DSA’S DANGEROUS FINE PRINT. THEY'RE COMING FOR MILLIONAIRES (AND YOU) Moore also questioned whether wealthy advocates of wealth redistribution should voluntarily give up more of their own assets and challenged progressive leaders to explain why they continue to benefit from capitalism while criticizing it. "I think the capital H is for hypocrisy here, and if these people really believed and share the wealth policies that they keep espousing, maybe they could start with themselves," Moore said. "Maybe they could sell some of these assets and give the money to the poor, but it turns out, by the way, that liberal socialists tend to be the least generous in terms of charitable giving. There was a very famous book on this. So it turns out that free market capitalists tend to be very generous in sharing their wealth, but not so much so democratic socialists." DEPROGRAMMED: FORMER DSA INSIDER REVEALS ‘FRIGHTENING’ SOCIALIST AGENDA DROVE HIM FROM ‘EXTREME’ IDEOLOGY The economist said some socialists try to conceal their wealth to appeal more to the public. "They try to hide their wealth from Americans so they can pretend like they are working-class people," Moore said. "But if you look at the people who are really at the head of the democratic socialist movement and the people who are spending a lot of money, those tend to be very rich people themselves. This is, as I said before, this is the only country where you can get rich off of attacking the free market capitalism system, which really creates the wealth in the United States in the first place. It's the reason why so many people come to this country from socialist countries and they get here and they say they don't understand why anyone would want to have more socialism in America when they've seen it fail in their own country." articles.title: 4 American tourists dead after building explosion in Greece
articles.summary: The mayor of Athens said the explosion was likely caused by a gas leak.
articles.body:
Four Americans were among the six people who died after an explosion and building collapse in Athens' tourist district of Plaka near the Acropolis on Friday, officials said.

The blast, which occurred at dawn on Friday, was likely caused by a gas leak, according to Athens Mayor Haris Doukas.

The two other people killed were an elderly British man and his Greek wife who lived on the second floor of the three-story building, Greece's state broadcaster ERT reported.

The American family of four had been renting an apartment on the first floor and were preparing to go to the airport hours later Friday for their return to the United States when the blast occurred, according to the Kathimerini newspaper.

The explosion brought down the residential building and damaged properties and vehicles along the street. Two other women were injured from an adjacent building on Lysikratous Street, fire brigades said, according to the Associated Press.

The New York Times reported that the U.S. family was composed of a couple, their son and his girlfriend. Greek authorities did not immediately give their identities, ages or where in the U.S. they came from.

On Saturday, AFP reporters saw mechanical diggers moving debris at the site and thermal-imaging cameras deployed.

"We are talking about an incredible disaster," Doukas said.

Two nearby buildings were left in a dangerous state, he added, with inspections underway "to determine if they can remain standing or if they also have to be demolished."

The owner of the ground-floor apartment, Mathaios Artavanis, told the Kathimerini daily he was absent at the time of the blast. He said he had tried afterward to contact the U.K.-Greek couple who lived there, without success.

Video footage from the scene showed rubble strewn across the street, with parked cars smashed by falling debris. The people rescued by the fire department from the adjacent building were all tourists, resident Andreas Martzaklis said.

The pastor of a nearby church said this Sunday's service would be held outdoors because of damage to the church.

A year ago, locals in the Plaka neighborhood had warned the city and utility companies about the risk of gas leaks or short circuits, according to a letter by the residents' association published by Kathimerini.

The residents had urged a fire drill to identify possible weaknesses in the emergency response plans for the district.

A citizens' group said on social media that one resident in the street where the explosion happened had alerted authorities after smelling a possible gas leak.

The neighborhood is one of Athens' most popular tourist areas. The nearby Acropolis, one of Greece's best-known landmarks, welcomed 4.6 million visitors last year.

articles.body: Elijah Hemingway, the 32-year-old man accused of fatally stabbing a Pittsburgh-area doctor inside his home, had previously made bizarre claims during an encounter with police in Florida, including telling officers that he was the reincarnation of ancient Egyptian ruler King Tutankhamun, according to body-camera footage obtained by WPXI and reported by the New York Post.Hemingway is accused of breaking into the Edgewood, Pennsylvania, home of Dr Idris Evans in the early hours of Thursday and attacking Evans and his wife while they were sleeping. articles.title: The Kennedy Center is a sacred space bigger than any name
articles.summary: There are buildings we admire for their architecture, institutions we respect for their history, and then there are places that acquire something far more
articles.body: There are buildings we admire for their architecture, institutions we respect for their history, and then there are places that acquire something far more difficult to define.Over generations, they absorb the aspirations, emotions and creative energy of the people who pass through them until the physical structure becomes almost secondary to what it represents. The Kennedy Center is one of those places.For decades, the Kennedy Center has served as a temple of the performing arts, a place where artists from around the world have aspired to perform. Its importance, however, does not come simply from its magnificent architecture or its location overlooking the Potomac. It comes from what has happened on its stages and from the generations of artists who have stood beneath its lights. The building is only the vessel. What makes it extraordinary is the collective human energy that has accumulated within it.I had the privilege of experiencing that energy firsthand through UTSAV, a festival that we produced for several years at the Kennedy Center to introduce Western audiences to some of India’s greatest treasures of classical music and dance.More than 100 artists from India had the opportunity to grace the stages of the Kennedy Center, many of them carrying traditions that had been passed from teacher to student for centuries. They did not arrive simply as performers. They arrived carrying the history, discipline, spirituality and cultural memory of an ancient civilization.Watching these artists perform at the Kennedy Center, I began to appreciate something that many artists who have performed there have expressed in their own way: there is a feeling associated with that stage that is difficult to replicate anywhere else. It is not simply the acoustics or the architecture, and it cannot be explained by the prestige of the institution alone. There is a sense that the artist is entering a space that has already been touched by generations of extraordinary human beings who devoted their lives to their craft.That sentiment is not unique to the Kennedy Center. Anyone who has spent time around legendary venues such as Carnegie Hall or the Sydney Opera House understands that their greatness cannot be explained by the physical structures themselves.READ: Sreedhar Potarazu | The color we choose as independent Indians (August 15, 2026)What distinguishes these places is the collective energy created by the artists who have performed there and the audiences who have shared those experiences. A musician brings the accumulated discipline of a lifetime to the stage. A dancer brings years of physical sacrifice and mastery. A singer brings not only a voice but a lifetime of emotion and inspiration .. Each performance adds another layer to the history of the space.Over time, those individual contributions become something collective. The stage begins to carry an echo of everyone who has stood upon it, and the audience becomes part of that memory as well. That is why artists often speak about legendary venues with a reverence that goes beyond the physical space. They understand that when they perform there, they are joining a lineage that began long before them and will continue long after they are gone.That is what makes the Kennedy Center a sacred space.Its sacredness does not come from any individual associated with it. It comes from the cumulative contribution of thousands of artists and millions of audience members who have participated in its history. It comes from the young performer who spent a lifetime dreaming of standing on that stage, from the established artist who arrived carrying decades of experience, and from the audience member who sat quietly in the dark and was moved by something that could not have been communicated in any other way.This is why I believe the significance of the Kennedy Center is much bigger than any one person. Institutions that become symbols of human achievement ultimately transcend the individuals who temporarily lead, govern, support or represent them. People come and go, administrations change, boards change, artistic leadership changes and names may change, but the cultural legacy created over generations belongs to something much larger.READ: Sreedhar Potarazu | For leaders like Fauci and McConnell, silence is not an option (August 6, 2026)It belongs to the arts themselves.When we brought Indian classical artists to the Kennedy Center through UTSAV, the purpose was never simply to put performances on a prestigious stage. We wanted to create a bridge between cultures and allow Western audiences to experience traditions that had evolved thousands of miles away. The Kennedy Center provided the setting in which those traditions could meet a new audience, and for a few hours, music and dance became a language that required no translation.The experience reinforced something that I have come to believe deeply: great cultural institutions are among the places where humanity reminds itself of what it is capable of. In an increasingly technological world, where so much of our lives can be quantified, automated and mediated through machines, the performing arts preserve something that remains fundamentally human.A performance is not simply a sequence of sounds or movements. It is a human being communicating something that has been shaped by a lifetime of discipline, emotion, struggle, imagination and aspiration.That is why these institutions matter beyond entertainment. They are part of the cultural infrastructure of civilization.The Kennedy Center is therefore not simply a building in Washington. It is a living repository of human aspiration. Its stages have been touched by artists from different countries, cultures and generations, each contributing something that becomes part of the institution’s collective memory. The significance of that history cannot be reduced to the identity of any one person associated with the institution at a particular moment.We should instead ask what we want that legacy to mean for the generations that follow us. I hope a young dancer from India, a violinist from Japan, an opera singer from Italy or a young American actor can look toward the Kennedy Center and see a place where their own aspirations are possible. I hope artists from cultures that have never before been represented there can imagine bringing their traditions to that stage. And I hope audiences continue to enter those halls and encounter something that reminds them, despite all of our differences, of the extraordinary things human beings share.Perhaps that is ultimately what makes a place sacred. It is not who controls it or whose name is associated with it. It is what generations of people have created within it and what those creations mean to the people who come afterward.The Kennedy Center has accumulated decades of that energy. Every artist who has performed there has contributed something to its spirit, and every audience that has gathered to experience those performances has become part of its story. The result is something that no individual can claim as his or her own because it belongs to the collective human experience.That is the legacy worth protecting.Whatever name may appear on the outside, the essence of the Kennedy Center must remain bigger than anyone in it. It should remain a sanctuary where artists can bring the very best of themselves, where cultures can meet without borders, and where audiences can experience the unique power of sacred human expression.(By arrangement with The American Bazaar)You use AI every day. It has also asserted that all final decisions related to the SIR process were taken unanimously and had the approval of all three commissioners.The Congress has indicated that opposition parties may move a fresh impeachment motion against CEC Kumar in Parliament. articles.title: How Taiwan’s ‘silicon shield’ has kept it safe from China, indispensable to US in age of AI
articles.summary: The latest meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping has once again put Taiwan at the centre of the world's most
articles.body: The latest meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping has once again put Taiwan at the centre of the world's most consequential geopolitical and technology rivalry.Xi pressed Trump during their Washington talks to adopt what Beijing calls the "correct position" of opposing Taiwan independence, according to a Chinese readout. Taiwan rejected the demand, saying Beijing had no right to determine the island's future. The exchange came as Washington continues to balance its longstanding support for Taiwan with its broader effort to manage relations with Beijing.The Taiwan question, however, is about more than territory, military power or competing political claims. It is also about one of the most important foundations of the modern global economy: semiconductors.Taiwan produces the overwhelming majority of the world's most advanced chips, with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, or TSMC, at the centre of that ecosystem. These chips power smartphones, artificial intelligence systems, high-performance computers, data centres, automobiles and increasingly sophisticated military technologies.As Stanford University Hoover fellow Eyck Freymann told Rest of World, “The economic shock from a serious Taiwan disruption would dwarf anything we’ve seen in the postwar period.”The question is therefore not simply what would happen if China and Taiwan entered a military confrontation. It is why Taiwan became so important to the global chip industry, why TSMC is so difficult to replace, why the company depends on technology and suppliers across several countries, and why the US, China and India are all trying to reshape the semiconductor supply chain.The island that became a semiconductor chokepointSemiconductors are the building blocks of modern electronics. They allow computers to process information, smartphones to function, vehicles to operate sophisticated electronic systems and AI data centres to perform enormous numbers of calculations.But semiconductor manufacturing is not concentrated in one country. The supply chain is divided among economies with different strengths.The US has major capabilities in chip design, software and electronic design automation. Taiwan dominates advanced manufacturing. South Korea is a major force in memory. Japan is important for semiconductor materials and equipment. The Netherlands is home to ASML, the key supplier of advanced lithography systems.Taiwan's importance comes from the concentration of advanced manufacturing on the island. Government data says Taiwan accounts for more than 60% of global chip production and nearly 90% of advanced chips. TSMC is at the centre of that ecosystem.TSMC's scale illustrates why it is difficult to replace. In 2025, the company manufactured 12,682 products using 305 process technologies for 534 customers. Its chips served sectors including high-performance computing, smartphones, automobiles, the Internet of Things and consumer electronics. Its manufacturing capacity exceeded 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers during the year.The company therefore sits between some of the world's largest technology companies and the physical production of their chips.How Taiwan built its semiconductor advantageTaiwan's position was built over decades.In the 1970s, Taiwanese policymakers recognised that the island could not immediately compete with the US and Japan across the entire technology industry. Instead, it focused on specialised manufacturing capabilities and technology transfer.The Industrial Technology Research Institute, or ITRI, was established in 1973. Taiwan subsequently acquired semiconductor technology from the US through licensing arrangements and trained engineers overseas. The development of the Hsinchu Science Park, established in 1980, added another crucial component.Hsinchu brought together semiconductor companies, research institutions, universities, engineers and suppliers. Over time, this geographic concentration created an ecosystem in which companies could access skilled workers, equipment, suppliers and technical expertise.The decisive change came in 1987, when Morris Chang founded TSMC.Chang's idea was to separate chip design from chip manufacturing. Instead of designing and selling its own branded chips, TSMC would manufacture chips designed by other companies.The model became known as the pure-play foundry model.TSMC's business model allowed companies such as Nvidia and Qualcomm to concentrate on chip architecture and design without having to build and operate their own advanced fabs. At the same time, TSMC could focus entirely on manufacturing.The model also reduced concerns among customers that their manufacturing partner would compete with them in the chip market. TSMC says its exclusive focus on manufacturing customers' products was central to the pure-play foundry model.That division of labour helped create the modern fabless semiconductor industry and made TSMC a central manufacturing partner for some of the world's most valuable technology companies.Why TSMC is so difficult to replaceTSMC's advantage is not simply the buildings containing its fabs.A leading-edge semiconductor facility requires enormous capital investment, but a modern fab also depends on years of accumulated process knowledge, engineering expertise, equipment suppliers, chemicals, gases, utilities, logistics and specialist workers.Taiwan developed these capabilities around TSMC over several decades.The result is a dense industrial ecosystem that is difficult to reproduce simply by spending money on a new factory.TSMC is expanding outside Taiwan. It operates manufacturing facilities in Japan and China, has expanded its Arizona operations and is developing a specialty technology fab in Dresden, Germany. But the company continues to invest heavily in Taiwan, including multiple 2nm facilities and advanced packaging capacity.That is why governments seeking greater semiconductor security are generally trying to create additional capacity rather than assuming that Taiwan's entire ecosystem can quickly be recreated elsewhere.Taiwan's 'silicon shield'Taiwan's semiconductor dominance has also acquired a geopolitical dimension.The idea of a "silicon shield" was explicitly described by former Taiwanese president Tsai Ing-wen in a 2021 Foreign Affairs article. The basic argument is that Taiwan's importance to the global economy creates a form of mutual dependence.A major conflict that disrupted Taiwan's chip industry would not hurt Taiwan alone. It would affect economies and companies that rely on its semiconductor output.But the shield is not an absolute guarantee of security.Eyck Freymann, author of Defending Taiwan: A Strategy to Prevent War With China, has argued that the concept can be overstated. China would not necessarily need to seize TSMC's factories to disrupt the semiconductor supply chain.A blockade, quarantine or other form of coercion could interfere with the movement of chips out of Taiwan even if the factories themselves continued operating.That distinction is important. Semiconductor production depends not only on fabs but also on electricity, water, equipment, chemicals, logistics, shipping routes and international workers and suppliers.A disruption to those systems could therefore affect output without physically destroying a fab.China wants semiconductor self-relianceChina's semiconductor strategy is closely linked to its broader technology and national-security objectives.Beijing has invested heavily in reducing dependence on foreign semiconductor technology, while Washington has imposed restrictions on China's access to advanced chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment.Chinese companies including Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation and Huawei have developed domestic capabilities, while Beijing has pushed for greater self-sufficiency across the semiconductor value chain.China has made progress, particularly in mature and increasingly advanced manufacturing, but the leading edge remains difficult because of restrictions on advanced equipment and technology.The contest is particularly important because the most advanced chips depend on highly specialised manufacturing equipment that China has historically had limited access to.The EUV bottleneckAt the centre of the advanced-chip race is extreme ultraviolet, or EUV, lithography.EUV systems use light with a wavelength of 13.5 nanometres to print extremely small patterns on semiconductor wafers. The technology is critical to producing some of the most advanced generations of chips.This is where the Netherlands enters the semiconductor story.Dutch company ASML is the world's key supplier of EUV lithography systems. ASML does not manufacture chips. It makes the machines used by chipmakers to manufacture them.A modern EUV system combines precision optics, lasers, vacuum systems, mirrors, sensors and thousands of components supplied through a highly specialised international network. German company Carl Zeiss is central to the optical systems, while suppliers in the US, Japan and elsewhere contribute other components and materials.The result is a semiconductor supply chain in which no single country controls every critical technology.Taiwan provides leading-edge manufacturing. The Netherlands provides critical lithography equipment. The US has major strengths in chip design and related technologies. Japan supplies important materials and equipment. South Korea dominates parts of the memory market.ASML and TSMC are already working on the next generation of EUV technology. In September 2026, the companies announced an initiative to transition the industry towards 12-inch photomasks for High NA EUV. TSMC intends to use ASML's High NA technology in high-volume manufacturing for advanced nodes from 2030, while the initiative targets a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031 and advanced-node production readiness by 2033.That relationship shows how difficult it is for any one country to become completely independent in semiconductor technology.China's EUV challengeChina's attempt to develop its own EUV capability has therefore become one of the most closely watched parts of the semiconductor race.Reuters reported in December 2025 that China had developed a prototype EUV lithography machine at a secure facility in Shenzhen. The machine was reportedly capable of generating EUV light but was not yet capable of producing advanced chips. Reuters also reported that former ASML engineers had been recruited and that China had used components obtained from older systems and secondary markets.The distinction is important. Producing EUV light is not the same as developing a commercially viable EUV system capable of manufacturing advanced chips reliably and at scale.ASML's position was built over decades of research, engineering and collaboration with a vast supplier network. China therefore faces the additional challenge of converting research breakthroughs into reliable industrial production.But the effort demonstrates why export controls cannot be viewed simply as a permanent technological barrier. They can restrict access to critical technologies while also encouraging efforts to develop alternatives.The US wants to reduce its dependenceWashington faces a different version of the same problem.The US has enormous strengths in semiconductor design and technology, but advanced manufacturing has historically been concentrated in East Asia. As competition with China intensified, that dependence became a national-security concern.The US response has included export controls on advanced semiconductor technology going to China and incentives to expand manufacturing capacity inside the country.The CHIPS and Science Act provided incentives for companies including TSMC to build US manufacturing capacity. TSMC has since expanded its Arizona plans substantially. In July 2026, the company pledged a further $100 billion investment in Arizona, taking its planned US investment to $165 billion.The objective is not necessarily to eliminate Taiwan's importance. It is to create additional capacity so that a disruption in Taiwan does not automatically become a disruption to the entire global semiconductor industry.But the same problem remains: a fab is only one part of the ecosystem.Taiwan is also becoming more important to AIThe rapid expansion of artificial intelligence has made Taiwan's position even more important.AI systems require enormous amounts of computing power, and the most advanced AI accelerators depend on leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging.TSMC is deeply embedded in this supply chain. Its 2025 annual report said advanced technologies, defined as 7nm and more advanced processes, accounted for 74% of its total wafer revenue.Taiwan is also expanding advanced packaging capabilities. In September 2026, construction began on a new advanced packaging industrial park in Kaohsiung anchored by TSMC, with facilities planned for technology validation and talent development.The semiconductor race is therefore no longer only about making smaller transistors. Advanced packaging, memory, lithography, chip design and manufacturing are increasingly interconnected, particularly as AI demand grows.Taiwan's chips as diplomatic leverageTaiwan's semiconductor position has also created a new form of economic and diplomatic leverage.In 2025, Taipei announced proposed restrictions on semiconductor exports to South Africa amid a dispute over Taiwan's representative office there. The proposed controls were subsequently suspended after South Africa agreed to negotiations.The measures therefore did not become a lasting export-control regime. But the episode demonstrated that Taiwan's position in the global chip supply chain can potentially be used as a diplomatic tool.As Wen-ti Sung of the Atlantic Council's Global China Hub said in the material supplied for this story, “By utilizing Taiwan’s position in the global chip supply chain, this looks like Taipei’s attempt at building an autonomous deterrent on the world stage.”He added: “Going forward, other governments will be looking at this example and considering not only Taiwan’s carrots but also its potential sticks.”The episode also showed the limits of such leverage. The immediate economic impact was limited because South Africa represented only a small share of Taiwan's semiconductor exports.Where India standsIndia enters the semiconductor race from a different starting point.Its strongest links have traditionally been chip design, engineering, software and electronics services, while large-scale advanced fabrication has remained a major gap.That is beginning to change.Qualcomm's 2nm chip design tape-out, completed through its engineering centres in Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad, is an example of India's growing role in advanced chip development. But a tape-out is a design milestone, not manufacturing. The 2nm chip itself will be fabricated overseas.According to government data, India accounts for nearly 20% of the global semiconductor chip-design workforce and hosts about 7% of semiconductor-domain global capability centres.The government is attempting to build on that design advantage through the India Semiconductor Mission.Semicon 1.0, approved in 2021 with an outlay of Rs 76,000 crore, created support for semiconductor fabs, compound semiconductors, ATMP/OSAT facilities and chip-design companies. The government says 12 semiconductor manufacturing units have been approved, involving cumulative investment of more than Rs 1.64 lakh crore. It also says 24 chip-design projects have been approved and more than 300 chip designs have been developed through the wider ecosystem.India is also developing fabrication and packaging capabilities. Tata Electronics' Dholera project in Gujarat is intended to establish domestic silicon fabrication capacity, while projects involving Micron, Tata Electronics, CG Power and Kaynes are expanding assembly, testing and packaging capabilities.The next phase is Semicon 2.0, approved in July 2026 with an outlay of Rs 1,27,500 crore. It expands the focus to six areas: chip design, machines and materials, new fabs, advanced packaging, research and talent.The stakes are rising with domestic demand. India's semiconductor market is projected to reach $110 billion by FY2030 and exceed $200 billion by FY2035. India spent almost $150 billion on semiconductor product imports between FY2017 and FY2025.India's partnership with the Netherlands mattersIndia's strategy is not to build every part of the semiconductor chain independently. It is also to connect with established global technology ecosystems.The Netherlands and ASML are important to that strategy because advanced semiconductor manufacturing depends on sophisticated lithography technology.The Tata-PSMC relationship links India's emerging fabrication capacity with Taiwan's manufacturing expertise, while India's engagement with ASML connects it to the Netherlands' semiconductor equipment ecosystem.India is also seeking to build capabilities in equipment, materials, packaging and other specialised parts of the supply chain. Semicon 2.0 explicitly includes machines and materials alongside fabs, design, packaging, research and talent.India is therefore not trying to become another Taiwan overnight. Its immediate advantage is design and engineering, while fabrication, equipment, materials and advanced packaging are still developing.The semiconductor map is becoming a map of geopolitical powerThe global semiconductor industry is now a network of interdependent countries.Taiwan has TSMC and leading-edge manufacturing.The Netherlands has ASML and critical lithography technology.The US has major chip-design companies, software and semiconductor technologies.Japan supplies important materials and equipment.South Korea has enormous strength in memory and advanced manufacturing.China has a vast electronics manufacturing base and is investing heavily in semiconductor self-reliance.India has major engineering and design capabilities and is building manufacturing, packaging and materials capacity.No single country controls the entire chain.That interconnectedness has made advanced chips cheaper and more widely available, but it has also created concentration risks. A disruption at one critical point can affect industries far beyond semiconductors.The Taiwan question is also a technology questionThis is why Taiwan remains central to the US-China relationship.Beijing's claim over Taiwan, Washington's policy towards Taipei, Chinese military activity around the island and Taiwan's own political position are all part of the geopolitical equation. But beneath that lies another contest: control over the technologies that underpin the global economy.Taiwan's semiconductor industry gives the island an outsized position because it became indispensable at one critical point in the global technology chain.TSMC's success was built through decades of industrial policy, technology transfer, engineering expertise, supplier networks and a business model that separated chip design from manufacturing.That concentration now creates both strength and vulnerability.China wants alternatives. The US wants additional capacity. Europe and Japan want more resilient supply chains. India is building its own semiconductor ecosystem.The result is a gradual shift from a highly globalised semiconductor supply chain towards one increasingly shaped by national security and geopolitical considerations.For Taiwan, the challenge is to remain technologically ahead while preserving the ecosystem that made its semiconductor industry so difficult to replicate.For the rest of the world, the challenge is to reduce dependence on any single geographic centre without dismantling the global system that made advanced chips possible.And for India, the opportunity is not necessarily to replace Taiwan, but to become another important link in a semiconductor chain that is increasingly central to economic power, national security and geopolitics.You use AI every day. articles.title: As Trump hugs Xi and plugs Sharif, India feels the squeeze
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: The clearest sign yet of a widening US-India diplomatic rift came this weekend from the White House and the United
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: The clearest sign yet of a widening US-India diplomatic rift came this weekend from the White House and the United Nations, where India was denouncing Pakistan for what it called a litany of “falsehoods” and “deceit,” even as US President Donald Trump appeared to give those very claims a presidential imprimatur.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had used his UN General Assembly address to revive Islamabad’s account of the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, crediting Trump with a “timely intervention” that, he said, prevented a wider war. On Friday night, shortly after China’s President Xi Jinping had departed for Beijing, Trump posted an 87-second excerpt of Sharif’s speech on Truth Social without comment. The clip included Sharif’s praise of Trump and Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir.The timing was striking. India had just exercised its Right of Reply, with First Secretary Petal Gahlot accusing Islamabad of peddling “falsehoods” and “deceit” and describing Pakistan as a “puppet” regime. New Delhi has also rejected Trump’s repeated assertion that he mediated the cessation of hostilities in May 2025, saying the fighting was halted after direct military-to-military communication between India and Pakistan.For India, however, the larger concern may be less about one Truth Social post than about a pattern. The Xi visit to Washington this week appeared to underscore how dramatically the strategic geometry of US foreign policy has shifted. Rather than organizing its Asia policy principally around building India as a counterweight to China – a two-decade old Washington objective that resulting in an “Indo-Pacific” focused QUAD – the Trump White House increasingly appears willing to deal with Beijing as a peer whose cooperation is indispensable, and whose confrontation carries costs Trump is reluctant to incur.Following the Xi visit, Washington and Beijing extended their trade truce and agreed on tariff reductions covering $30 billion of less-sensitive goods in each direction, according reports in the Chinese media. They also operationalized bilateral boards on trade and investment and agreed to pursue an artificial-intelligence dialogue.Analysts say none of this amounts to a formal US-China condominium, and deep disagreements over Taiwan, technology, trade and strategic competition remain. But the emerging arrangement has prompted comparisons with a de facto G-2: Washington and Beijing managing their rivalry directly while other powers, including India, find themselves having to adjust to decisions made in a room in which they are not present.“One totally unsurprising consequence of this US-China trade truce is that Trump is not even thinking about implementing the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions legislation he just signed, which would have required penalizing China's support for Russia's war machine,” Tom Malinowski a former New Jersey lawmaker noted, even as Republicans close to Trump have been champing at the bit to punish New Delhi. The Graham bill, signed by Trump on Sept. 18, gives the president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries that continue buying Russian crude or natural gas under specified conditions. The law specifically covers countries among the five largest Russian oil or gas importers that make new purchases, as well as countries identified among the top facilitators of sanctions evasion.India is plainly exposed to that provision, as is China. Yet the contrast in Trump’s handling of the two relationships has become difficult for New Delhi to ignore: Beijing is being courted into a new economic accommodation even as India faces the prospect of punitive trade action.The message was reinforced this week by a senior State Department official who said the Graham law gives Trump “a new tool in his toolbox,” while emphasizing that its use is not automatic. The official pointed to a broad national-security waiver but added that Washington expects India to help the US end the Ukraine war.More revealing was the official's description of what Washington now wants from India: not necessarily strategic alignment against China, but access to the enormous Indian energy market. “We are looking to also become a huge source of India's energy needs,” the official was quoted as saying, pointing to expanding US hydrocarbon exports and urging faster diversification away from Russian supplies.All this is consequential because for two decades the bipartisan American strategy had been to help India acquire the economic, military and technological heft to balance China's rise. As recently as May, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who will be back in New Delhi in October, was describing India as one of America's most important strategic partners, while US officials continued to characterize New Delhi as a critical Indo-Pacific counterweight. The language now coming from Washington is noticeably more transactional.For New Delhi, the resulting unease is not simply about tariffs or Pakistan. It is about whether a strategic partnership painstakingly built across successive administrations is being replaced by a transactional relationship in which China is too powerful to punish, Pakistan is useful to cultivate, and India is expected to accommodate. And as New Delhi watched Washington kiss up to Beijing as an indispensable peer and embrace a country New Delhi views as a terrorism sponsor, the strategic space India once occupied in the American imagination appeared to be shrinking.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Beach and his more than 100 teammates from Tennessee’s Tickle College of Engineering were selected to compete in the 2026 EcoCAR Innovation Challenge against 19 other universities from across North America. The four-year program, administered by the U.S. Department of Energy and Argonne National Laboratory, and sponsored by car manufacturers General Motors and Stellantis, tasks college students with developing innovative and energy-efficient next-generation solutions for the automotive industry, using emerging technologies, artificial intelligence, connected and automated vehicle systems and advanced propulsion. articles.title: Florida couple sues Jacksonville’s Brown Fertility Clinic, alleging wrong sperm was used in IVF after baby’s blood type raises questions and a DNA test reveals husband isn’t biological father
articles.summary: A Florida couple is suing a Jacksonville fertility clinic after they say a routine blood test raised questions about their baby’s parentage, eventually
articles.body: A Florida couple is suing a Jacksonville fertility clinic after they say a routine blood test raised questions about their baby’s parentage, eventually leading to a DNA test that allegedly showed the husband was not the child’s biological father.Natalie and Josh Strong filed a medical negligence lawsuit against Brown Fertility Clinic in Duval County, Florida, on September 17, along with multiple clinic staff members, according to public court records viewed by PEOPLE. The couple alleges that the clinic used the wrong man’s sperm during their IVF treatment.Florida couple says baby’s blood type raised the first red flagNatalie said she gave birth to a healthy baby girl, Ava, in spring 2025. However, according to the couple, concerns emerged after routine blood work showed that their daughter had a B-positive blood type.Natalie is O-negative, while Josh is A-negative. The couple said they were initially unable to understand how their daughter could have a B-positive blood type given their blood types.Josh, who works as a nurse, immediately questioned the result.“Josh is a nurse, so immediately he said, ‘Well, how does that correlate?’” Natalie said, according to NBC Miami.The couple said they repeated the baby’s blood test and also had their own blood types checked again to rule out the possibility of a testing error.“And no one could figure it out. We tested her blood type again, and then we even [were] like, ‘Well, maybe one of our blood types is wrong’ from when he was in the military,” Natalie said. “So we tested his again and mine, and everyone was correct. So there was absolutely no chance that Ava should be B-positive with two negative blood types.”DNA test allegedly showed Josh was not the biological fatherThe couple said a subsequent DNA test revealed that Josh was not Ava’s biological father.According to the lawsuit, the Strongs believe the discrepancy was the result of an alleged error at Brown Fertility Clinic involving the sperm used during their IVF treatment. The allegations have not been established in court.The clinic did not immediately respond to PEOPLE’s request for comment.For Natalie and Josh, the discovery has added complicated emotions to what they expected to be a joyful experience of becoming parents.“We are devastated. I mean, this is gonna affect us for the rest of our lives. We gotta figure out how we’re gonna tell [our child] one day, and it took away the euphoria of having a baby,” Natalie said, according to NBC Miami.The couple said they have not received an explanation from the fertility clinic about what allegedly happened.Couple says they are dealing with grief, anger and loveJosh said the situation has brought a range of emotions as the couple continues to navigate life with their daughter.“You do have sadness and anger, and in the same day you also have joy and love. It’s just a lot to deal with, but we love her very much,” he told NBC Miami.Their attorney, Benjamin Ikuta of Fertility Law Group, described the alleged consequences of the incident as lasting and significant.“The emotional consequences are almost impossible to describe,” Ikuta said in a statement to the publication.“Joshua was deprived of the biological fatherhood he endured surgery [for] and paid the clinic to achieve. Natalie has had to confront the fact that an unknown man’s genetic material was used to create a pregnancy inside her body without her knowledge or consent. ... These are permanent injuries that no apology or accounting adjustment can undo,” he continued.Ikuta said the couple filed the lawsuit not only seeking accountability but also hoping to obtain answers that could potentially prevent similar incidents from affecting other families.Attorneys say lawsuit seeks answers from fertility clinicRob Marcereau, another Fertility Law Group attorney representing the Strongs, alleged that Brown Fertility Clinic has not provided an explanation for the situation.“Brown Fertility has ‘refused to provide any explanation for what happened. This lawsuit will hold Brown accountable and force them to provide answers,’” Marcereau said.The lawsuit is now proceeding in Duval County. The allegations made by the Strongs and their attorneys remain claims in a pending legal case, and the clinic has not publicly responded to the allegations at the time of publication.You use AI every day. articles.body: Washington is under siege. From rude reporters to pesky judges to ‘dum(b)’ lawmakers. And that headless Iranian regime that refuses to surrender despite threats of annihilation.But worry not. The commander-in-chief has monumental plans to make America safe again with drones, snipers and a whole lotta bang bangs stashed here there and everywhere across the town.His controversial fancy new $400 million ballroom, now coming up fast and furious on White House grounds after being green lighted by the Supreme Court on a technicality, will serve as a military complex with a bunker underneath and a big beautiful drone port on the top.And his triumphal arch envisioned as a project to honor America’s 250th anniversary, too would now be converted into a “top grade military complex … to house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers.”“There will be no facility like this anywhere in the world,” boasted the POTUS claiming that his new plan came at the “strong request” of the U.S. military without saying what the arch, to be erected between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery, would protect.National security remains DonaldTrump’s secret weapon. He has used it time and again to advance his pet projects and demolish his pet peeves from windmills to ‘fake news’ posing inconvenient questions and scooping embarrassing leaks.After citing it as a reason to pause the construction of wind farms off the East Coast, Trump argued his ban on CNN, MS Now and Politico entering the White House grounds too was necessary because they posed a national security threat.But a federal judge “sadly, appointed by ‘TRUMP’” did not buy the national security threat argument and restored their White House access for now. And the White House TV pool, which had for once resorted to a boycott of White House coverage to deprive Trump of the oxygen of attention he craves, too was back on the job.Yet in a latest escalation with news media, the White House still blocked CNN, which was scheduled to fly with Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, from Air Force One.Earlier, outdoing himself, Trump told world leaders at the United Nations Tuesday that he had a decision to make on Iran: strike a deal with Tehran or “annihilate the Islamic republic.”“Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever ‌was before?” …or “Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” he thundered even as the two sides kept talking on the sidelines.In a defiant speech next day, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian vowed his country would defend itself until “its last breath,” but he too left the door open for negotiations with the U.S.“It must be understood by Mr. Trump and those who seek to bully us that we are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force,” he said directly naming his adversary.Back in Washington, Trump again likened calls to slow development of artificial intelligence as a “globalist scheme” hatched by the same forces he blamed for warnings of climate change.Part of the answer, he said, was to change its name. Henceforth it would cease to be called “artificial” (“it makes it sound fake – and it’s not fake”) and would be called “super intelligence” in all U.S. government documents.“Welcome to the new world of super intelligence,” he posted after holding a poll between ‘Superior’ and ‘Extreme Intelligence’ on Truth Social after knocking out ‘Supreme Intelligence’… “because of its relationship to the Supreme Court.”Earlier, brushing away suggestions to slow down AI technology, Trump announced plans to appoint an artificial intelligence czar and create an “AI Force” to help monitor the technology.“I am forming the AI Force, much like I did Space Force, which has been a tremendous SUCCESS, in my First Term. To that end, I will be announcing, in the near future, the AI ‘Czar’ – Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!” Trump wrote on Truth Social.Vowing that his administration “will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry,” Trump suggested that any “bad actors” in AI industry could be addressed by criminal and civil systems of justice.“AI is the next Industrial Revolution, or Internet, but will be even larger and more impactful, possibly as much as 25% of our Country’s GDP,” Trump predicted, concluding that the U.S. is “leading China, and the rest of the World, and I intend to keep it that way”.Then as Chinese president Xi Jinping came calling for a first State visit in 11 years, Trump greeted him with pomp and ceremony and a mandatory stop at the “legendary Presidential Walk of Fame” with his predecessor represented by an autopen. “This is the autopen… it’s Biden.” he told an amused Xi.It wasn’t clear what the summit achieved, but Trump described it as a “very productive meeting with President Xi for both the U.S.A. and China” with at least one tangible outcome.“Like almost everyone else, he seemed to like calling the poorly and inaccurately named Artificial Intelligence to a far more accurate and important name, SUPER INTELLIGENCE. That would be “SUPER!”’ he posted on Truth Social.Earlier, standing in the White House’s Grand Foyer Xi said both the U.S. and China “have the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control.”But who will keep the world safe from the Don tilting at windmills!(By arrangement with The American Bazaar)You use AI every day. articles.title: After 'big talk' on 'Super Intelligence' with Xi, Trump rules out joint US-China effort to advance AI
articles.summary: United States president Donald Trump ruled out join efforts with China to advance AI after the two met and held discussions earlier this week, as Xi
articles.body: United States president Donald Trump ruled out join efforts with China to advance AI after the two met and held discussions earlier this week, as Xi Jinping visited Washington.While Trump said that both leaders agreed on renaming it to "Super intelligence", SI (a name Trump has pushed for recently), he dismissed the idea of integration. "We had a big talk on SI," Trump told reporters at the White House, using his preferred name of super intelligence."What they want to do is stop our progress because we're leading China by a lot, and we're going to keep it that way. We didn't spend that much time talking about it," he added.Defending his stance, the US president reiterated, "he did not want to "integrate" AI initiatives with China because of US dominance. "I would rather not integrate because we're leading by a lot," he said, adding: "When you're leading, you don't open it up to each other".This comes a day after Trump hailed "productive meeting" between him and Xi where he said "everyone" agreed on the renaming. The two leaders agreed to use the term “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” for applicable emerging technologies.The US and China also agreed on establishing the US-China Super Intelligence Dialogue to exchange views on the risks and benefits linked to such technologies, with the next exchange scheduled for November 2026. They also agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel for incidents involving super intelligence. The two countries also agreed to launch the dialogue on AI under an eight-point consensus reached after bilateral talks, according to China’s state news agency Xinhua.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Bill Maher praised Donald Trump's tough-on-crime persona on "Real Time," saying the "f---around-and-find-out president" sent a message to bad guys.
articles.body: Comedian Bill Maher offered surprising praise for President Donald Trump's handling of crime Friday, telling his audience that the president's tough-guy persona may have played a role in a nationwide drop in violent crime. "It's not just drug crime that's way down, it's all crime," Maher said during Friday’s episode of HBO’s "Real Time," adding, "And again, probably much of it is not political. It's because you can't move two inches in America without being tracked, photographed, and followed by a Flock camera." According to the late-night host, the president is a "bad a--" and it's childish to pretend" his tough on crime stance isn't having an impact. Maher went on to credit both Democratic policies and Trump with contributing to lower nationwide crime rates. MAHER MOCKS LIBERALS FOR STILL PANICKING ABOUT TRUMP'S ANTICS, PERSONALITY AFTER 10 YEARS "It's also because when Democrats expand the safety net, there are less desperate people," Maher said. "And because Trump is a bad a--." Maher added that while he does not "agree with many of [Trump’s] methods," he cannot argue that the president’s tough-on-crime approach has yielded successful results. TRUMP TO RALLY WITH NEW YORK POLICE IN HIGHLIGHTING HISTORIC COAST-TO-COAST VIOLENT CRIME DROP "Is doing it this way the right thing? No. But it's just childish to pretend that when you elect a f---around-and-find-out president, a no-more-Mr.-Nice-Guy, boot-in-your-a--, ‘V for Vendetta,’ kick-a-- and take names, say-hello-to-my-little-friend president, that's not going to have some effect on crime," he continued. "He has UFC fights on the lawn," Maher concluded. "I think the bad guys got the message." KASH PATEL TO TOUT 'LARGEST' YEAR-TO-YEAR VIOLENT CRIME DROP IN US HISTORY According to the FBI’s Crime Data Explorer, reported violent crime nationwide fell 9% from June 2025 through May 2026. Robbery saw the steepest drop, at 19.4%, followed by murder at 18.7%, rape at 10% and aggravated assault at 6.2%. Retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent Jason Pack also pointed to the potential for bipartisan agreement on crime, telling Fox News Digital that "people may have strong disagreements with other parts of an agenda," but that "there can still be common ground around getting violent offenders off the street and making neighborhoods safer." CRIME IS FALLING, OFFICIALS SAY — VICTIMS CLAIM REPORTING ISN’T WORTH IT "You don’t have to wear somebody’s campaign button to admit when something appears to be working. That’s probably why you’re hearing even some of the president’s critics acknowledge what they’re seeing on crime," Pack said. He emphasized the need for collaboration among local, state and federal law enforcement to make a meaningful difference in fighting crime across the country. But most folks want the same things when they get home at the end of the day," Pack said, adding, "We may never get all the way back to the days when people left the front door unlocked, but folks ought to be able to feel secure in their own neighborhood and know violent offenders are being taken off the street. That’s not red or blue. It seems to me that’s red, white and blue." articles.title: Few licences, no records: Who makes up your bus crew?
articles.summary: Kochi private buses face safety concerns as many conductors lack licences and extra unaccounted staff, with crews racing, bullying motorists and clashing.
articles.body: Kochi: Fierce competition among private buses has turned the city’s roads into a dangerous arena, where motorists must pull over or risk being hit by crews in a day-long death race.Crew members with criminal antecedents make it deadlier. Violent confrontations are routine, yet authorities usually act only when CCTV footage exposes them.Central police on Thursday registered a case following a clash between the crews of two buses, Shalima and Akshay-Aleena. Shalima’s crew objected when Akshay-Aleena jumped its allotted slot and overtook them. The crew of Akshay-Aleena threatened them, and when Shalima’s owner intervened, he was beaten at High Court Junction on Thursday morning, leaving him with injuries under his eyes and a dislodged tooth.Also on Thursday, near the district court on Park Avenue Road, a bus’s persistent honking forced a car driver to pull left. When he tried to overtake the bus at a stop near the old corporation office, its driver allegedly swerved sharply right and hit the car.A day earlier, footage from Ravipuram showed a bus overtaking another from the left and mounting the footpath, nearly killing a pedestrian. On Thursday, Central police registered another case after a policeman spotted two buses racing at Madhava Pharmacy Junction.Many such incidents go unreported, as motorists whose vehicles are damaged often give up on complaining.When Aluva-Perumbadappu bus Sajimon was seized in Aug, it allegedly had over 300 challans, mostly pending. Muhammed Anzar, a bus cleaner recently arrested for threatening commuters in Kaloor and Thrikkakara, allegedly had around seven cases against him.Staff like these, on almost all buses, fall outside regulation. “Very few conductors on private buses hold a valid licence from transport department. On top of that, every bus has two or three additional staff. There is no accountability as to who these persons are and when and where they were employed,” said a senior motor vehicles department official.Some are specifically tasked with confronting rival crews during altercations. “For maximising business by reaching passenger-heavy spots first, drivers frequently race each other and bully other vehicles by driving dangerously,” the official said.The department cannot legally cancel permits over traffic challans alone and is severely short-staffed, he added. “We need special squads, at least one each in all constituencies of Ernakulam, to effectively monitor the buses.”Overcrowded buses often ply with their doors open. On Monday, a 31-year-old woman died after falling from a moving bus in North Paravur. In July, a 56-year-old nun died after being thrown out of a moving bus in Kozhippilly. Last Tuesday in Vypeen, Stivin (44) was hospitalised with a fractured elbow after a bus hit his two-wheeler head-on. In March last year, a 36-year-old woman on a two-wheeler was run over when trapped between two racing buses.Vyttila-based activist TN Prathapan says he now prefers KSRTC or Metro, fearing rash driving. He submitted a petition to transport commissioner a few days ago. “In the petition I said that arrangements must be made for the public to travel safely and without fear. The abusive language and physical fights among staff have become intolerable,” he said.KB Suneer of Private Bus Operators Association said most buses in serious incidents, including the Ravipuram bus, are not members of recognised associations. “Such buses, mostly operating on lease, make up 25-30% of those on the road,” he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news. articles.title: Gurgaon siblings go missing after mom’s scolding, found safe at temple
articles.summary: GURGAON: More than 50 police personnel scanned around 30 CCTV cameras and questioned local residents to trace two minor siblings, aged 12 and 13, who ran
articles.body: GURGAON: More than 50 police personnel scanned around 30 CCTV cameras and questioned local residents to trace two minor siblings, aged 12 and 13, who ran away from their home on Thursday after their mother scolded them. The children were found safe at a temple in Sector 37 on Friday, within 18 hours of a complaint being filed, police said.According to Gurgaon Police, the children's father, a native of Uttar Pradesh, approached Sector 10 police station on September 25 and informed that his 12-year-old and 13-year-old children were missing. Police registered a case under relevant sections and formed teams from Sector 10 police station and the Missing Persons Cell (West) to search for them.The teams checked around 30 CCTV cameras in the area and questioned local residents while searching for the siblings. Police traced the children on September 26 at Shani temple in Sector 37 and informed their family.During the inquiry, the children told police that they had left home after being scolded by their mother. They did not return home, spent the night sleeping in a park and later went to the temple in Sector 37.Police said the children were taken through the necessary procedures and counselled through the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). After completing the legal formalities, the police handed them over safely to their family."We appeal to parents and guardians to keep a close watch on young children. In such cases, people should immediately inform the nearest police station or post, or dial 112, if a child goes missing or is found lost or wandering", Sandeep Turan, police spokesperson said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: Citizens are our eyes and ears; their cooperation is indispensable: DCP Saravana
articles.summary: New Bhubaneswar DCP Saravana Vivek M prioritises community policing, trust, engagement, and strict accountability, with focus on cybercrime and fraud.
articles.body: Newly appointed Bhubaneswar DCPSaravana Vivek M, who assumed charge on Friday, speaks to TOI’sDebabrata Mohapatra about his priorities, public engagement and police accountabilityQ: How do you plan to align your policing strategy with the expectations of citizens?A: Public safety is at the heart of policing. We will make every effort to reach out to people, win their trust and strengthen their confidence in police. Citizens should feel comfortable approaching us. Our policing strategy will be guided by public feedback and community participation.Q: What steps will you take to improve police-public relations?A: We will neither shy away from the public nor scare them away. Citizens are our eyes and ears, and their cooperation is indispensable in maintaining law and order. I want to go one step beyond public expectations. Police stations will be encouraged to identify opportunities for regular engagement with residents, visit neighbourhoods frequently and participate in local programmes. We will also reach out to schools, colleges, offices and other institutions.Q: Your message for the personnel under your command?A: I strongly believe in teamwork. My message to all officers and personnel is simple -- work together and perform to the best of your abilities. Good work and outstanding service will be recognised and appreciated. Effective policing is possible only when there is mutual trust and cooperation within the force.Q: How will you ensure transparency and accountability within the police force?A: I will closely supervise the functioning of personnel engaged in public service delivery. I expect every member of the force to discharge their duties with discipline, honesty and professionalism. Any evidence of misconduct, corruption or indiscipline will be dealt with firmly. If any citizen faces corruption or is asked for a bribe, I would encourage them to report the matter to the vigilance authorities.Q: How would you like citizens to assess your performance?A: Ultimately, public satisfaction and trust will be the most important indicators of our success. If citizens feel safer, more confident and comfortable approaching the police, I would consider that a significant achievement.Q: How will the city police respond to evolving crime patterns, particularly cybercrime and financial fraud?A: Policing is evolving with changing challenges. articles.body: Thane: A 56-year-old police sub-inspector was allegedly fatally attacked by a history-sheeter during a late-night patrol in Pokhran 2 after the accused was confronted for creating a nuisance in a public place, police said.The incident occurred minutes before Friday midnight when a patrolling team, including PSI Kisan Bhoir, reached the area after noticing a commotion near a paan stall. TENNESSEE FANS EXCITED FOR TRUMP'S ATTENDANCE AT GAME VS TEXAS: 'I HOPE HE STAYS THE WHOLE GAME' It was brutal. But Knoxville is different. Tennessee is a different animal. Fans were told to get to the stadium hours before today's noon kickoff due to heightened security, and they listened. articles.title: Air India crash probe: Pilots' body seeks formal consideration of its tech submissions
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has urged the civil aviation ministry to ensure that its technical submissions on the Air India AI171
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has urged the civil aviation ministry to ensure that its technical submissions on the Air India AI171 crash are formally considered before the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) finalises its probe report.The AAIB investigation into the June 12, 2025 crash in Ahmedabad, which killed 260 people, is at an advanced stage.In a letter to civil aviation minister K Rammohan Naidu on Friday, FIP sought to be nominated as an “independent technical participant in the review of the draft AI171 final investigation report”.FIP said it had “reliably learnt that the government/ ministry has directed or is considering requiring the draft report to undergo examination by an independent committee before it is circulated/ finalised”. It said that if such a review mechanism is being constituted, the pilots' body should be formally nominated and represented as an independent technical stakeholder representing the professional pilot community.The federation also requested that its technical submissions receive formal and documented consideration before the final report is issued.The FIP had last week urged the AAIB to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of electrical-system evidence related to Boeing 787 aircraft as part of the AI171 investigation.The Air India Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner, registered as VT-ANB, crashed shortly after taking off from Ahmedabad for London Gatwick on June 12, 2025. Of the 242 people on board, 241 died, while 19 people on the ground were also killed. All 12 crew members died and one passenger survived.The aircraft, manufactured in 2013 and powered by GE engines, had flown 41,868 hours. Its Airworthiness Review Certificate was valid until May 23, 2026.In its latest update on the investigation, the AAIB said significant progress had been made and that the final report would be released after completion of all investigative activities and the required international review and consultation processes.The bureau has said the investigation team has examined technical, operational, organisational and human factors associated with the accident, without disclosing specific findings from the probe.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
